answers.explanation: MAIL FROM: and RCPT TO: are SMTP commands: the envelope. The rest are headers.
It shows the From: header. The envelope sender only shows up if you look at Return-Path.
The envelope delivers to them, while the headers everyone sees don't mention them.
RFC 5322, the Internet Message Format. SMTP itself is RFC 5321.
The first empty line ends the headers. The lone dot ends the whole message.
On top, so the newest hop is first.
The bottom header is the first hop, the top header the last.
It doesn't check at all, which is why spoofing is easy without SPF, DKIM, and DMARC.
Return-Path: holds the MAIL FROM: address, where bounces go.
